_README: Train a character LoRA on ComfyUI's native training nodes, then save the .safetensors.
ComfyUI API-format workflow. Node category: Cinematographer.
STATUS: NOT VERIFIED. This graph has never been executed, and NO LORA HAS BEEN
TRAINED. It was authored from the node schemas in ComfyUI master (see PROVENANCE) but
no ComfyUI instance and no GPU were available where it was written, so nothing here is
a claim that it runs or that it produces a usable adapter. What IS verified is
structural, and you can re-run it yourself:
python3 workflows/validate_graphs.py
That checks the file parses as JSON, that every node has class_type + inputs, that
every class_type is in a table of slot counts read from the node sources, that
every link resolves to an existing node id and a slot that node declares, that every
node supplies a legal number of inputs for its class_type, that the graph is acyclic,
and that every node is reachable from an output node. It does NOT check that ComfyUI
accepts the prompt. Treat the first run as a debugging session.
WHY THE BASE IS LTX 2.3 AND NOT AN IMAGE MODEL. A LoRA is not portable: it is a set of
low-rank deltas against one base's attention and projection weights, so it only loads
into the base it was trained on. The adapter this graph produces is consumed by
reshoot_ltx23_character.json, which loads it with LoraLoaderModelOnly in series with
the LTX 2.3 distilled LoRA -- therefore this graph trains on the LTX 2.3 22B
transformer. To train for a Flux-class or Qwen-Image base instead, swap nodes 3, 4 and
5 for that base's UNETLoader / DualCLIPLoader / VAELoader and drop learning_rate to
~1e-4 or lower; the dataset, training and saving wiring is unchanged. Do not expect one
adapter to serve both.
PROVENANCE. Node names, input names, slot counts and defaults were read from ComfyUI
master source, not guessed (read 2026-10-29):
comfy_extras/nodes_train.py     TrainLoraNode ('Train LoRA'), SaveLoRA
('Save LoRA Weights'), LossGraphNode
('Plot Loss Graph'), LoraModelLoader
comfy_extras/nodes_dataset.py   MakeTrainingDataset ('Make Training Dataset'),
LoadTrainingDataset, SaveTrainingDataset,
ResolutionBucket, LoadImageDataSetFromFolder
comfy_extras/nodes_primitive.py PrimitiveStringMultiline
comfy/weight_adapter/__init__.py  the `algorithm` options: LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, OFT
nodes.py                        UNETLoader, DualCLIPLoader, VAELoader
The upstream node ids are the class_types used below: in API format the id IS the
class_type, so 'Train LoRA' is TrainLoraNode and 'Save LoRA Weights' is SaveLoRA. The
display names are what the ComfyUI canvas shows; they are not what goes in this file.
Cross-checked against docs.comfy.org/built-in-nodes/TrainLoraNode.
TWO TRAPS, BOTH DOCUMENTED, BOTH AVOIDED HERE:
1. `steps` DEFAULTS TO 16. That is a smoke test -- it proves the graph executes, and
it produces an adapter that has learned essentially nothing. A character set wants
thousands of steps. This graph sets 2000, which is a starting point and not a
tuned number: watch the loss graph and the sample renders, not the step count.
2. `learning_rate` DEFAULTS TO 5e-4, which is SDXL-era. Flux-class and LTX-class
bases want ~1e-4 or lower; 5e-4 on a 22B transformer is how you get a fried
adapter that has memorised the reference set and destroys prompt adherence. This
graph sets 1e-4.
3. `bypass_mode` is set TRUE. Its own tooltip: 'adapters are applied via forward hooks
instead of weight modification. Useful for quantized models where weights cannot be
directly modified.' That is exactly our case -- node 3 loads an int8_convrot
checkpoint, and the LTX graphs this adapter feeds load int8_convrot and fp8_scaled
checkpoints. `training_dtype` is set to 'none' for the same reason: it preserves
the model's native compute dtype instead of overriding it. `quantized_backward` is
left at its default (false); turn it on only if backward through the quantized
matmul is what you need. This combination is read off the node's own tooltips -- it
is NOT taken from a worked example, and it is the single most likely thing in this
file to need adjusting on the first real run.
HONEST CAVEAT, and it belongs in the README rather than in a footnote. These training
nodes are marked EXPERIMENTAL in ComfyUI (is_experimental=True on every one of them) and
they shift between releases. The community default for serious character work is still
an external trainer -- ai-toolkit (MIT; FLUX.2 / Qwen-Image / Z-Image Turbo) or
diffusion-pipe. The native path is what makes this graph writable without a second
environment, a second toolchain or a second licence; it is not a claim that it is what
professionals use.
WHAT THIS GRAPH DOES NOT DO:
- It does not verify that the trained adapter holds the character's identity. Nothing
here measures facial identity; that needs a vision model and is out of scope for
this pack, exactly as the perceptual half of the framing rules is out of scope.
The loss curve is a training diagnostic, not an identity verdict.
- It does not caption per image. `texts` is one trigger-word caption repeated across
the whole set (MakeTrainingDataset repeats a length-1 text list for every image).
For per-image captions, put a .txt next to each image and use
LoadImageTextDataSetFromFolder in place of node 1.
- It does not bucket by resolution. bucket_mode is false and ResolutionBucket is not
in the chain. For a variable-aspect reference set, insert ResolutionBucket between
nodes 6 and 7 and set bucket_mode true on node 7; both slot counts are already in
the validator's table.
- It does not cache the encoded dataset. Insert SaveTrainingDataset after node 6 and
swap node 6 for LoadTrainingDataset on later runs to skip re-encoding. Also already
in the table.
WHAT IS VERIFIED vs NOT:
VERIFIED      valid JSON; class_type + inputs on every node; every link resolves to
an existing node id and a declared output slot; every node supplies a
legal number of inputs; acyclic; every node reachable from an output
node (SaveLoRA / Plot Loss Graph, which declare no outputs).
NOT VERIFIED  that ComfyUI accepts this prompt; that the weights below are installed;
that training converges; that the adapter holds identity. None of that
has been run.
REQUIRED NODE PACKS (custom):
NONE. Every class_type here is ComfyUI core, category model/training or model/loaders.
REQUIRED WEIGHTS (paths as ComfyUI names them; the three LTX names are the same ones
reshoot_ltx_crossview.json already uses, so this graph adds no new download):
models/diffusion_models/LTX2/ltx-2.3-22b-dev_transformer_only_int8_convrot.safetensors
models/text_encoders/gemma_3_12B_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors
models/text_encoders/LTX2/ltx-2.3_text_projection_bf16.safetensors
models/vae/ltx2/LTX23_video_vae_bf16.safetensors
INPUT: a folder of character reference stills under ComfyUI's input directory, named by
node 1's `folder` widget (placeholder: character_refs). PNG / JPG / JPEG / WEBP.
OUTPUT, and read this before looking for the file: SaveLoRA writes into ComfyUI's
OUTPUT directory, not into models/loras. With this prefix the adapter lands at
output/loras/cinematographer/character_2000_steps_00001_.safetensors
(SaveLoRA appends the step count when its optional `steps` input is wired, as it is
here, and its default prefix is the similarly misleading 'loras/ComfyUI_trained_lora').
To load the adapter you must move or copy it into models/loras/ first -- that is what
reshoot_ltx23_character.json expects. The loss graph PNG goes to the output directory
as well, under cinematographer/.
LICENCE. ComfyUI is GPL-3.0; the native training nodes are part of it. LTX 2.3 weights
are LTX-2.x Community (revenue-capped). No MiniMax H3 and no closed API anywhere in the
chain -- this graph trains entirely locally.
MEASURED: nothing. No timing, no VRAM figure, no loss curve, no adapter. The reference
app this pipeline is modelled on was demonstrated on a 96 GB GPU; training a rank-32
adapter on a 22B int8 transformer with gradient checkpointing and bypass mode is
expected to be far lighter than that, but that is an expectation, not a measurement.
